<!-- pr-reviewer: 5cbd2f176d03da227eb63f51dcd2506caa3d346e -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

## What looks good
- Triad keeps the right-handed program frame and only adds a note under the letter, once (first triad). The note follows `shown_setup` (the open operation's setup, else the active one) and not the first setup (`axis_note.rs`, `interact.rs`).
- The setup sheet reads `machine::of_setup(world, ctx)`, so it uses the machine of the setup being rendered. Standard machines print nothing.
- NC comment is safe: parenthesis form, plain uppercase text, `+` and `-` only, at most about 52 characters. It sits on its own block after the `O0001 (name)` line, so it is inside the program and after the O-word, where Fanuc and Haas accept comments.
- Only `fanuc_x.nc` and `haas_x.nc` changed, one added line each. No other golden moved, and standard-machine output is untouched (`invertedAxes` is `[]`).
- One wording table (`inverted_motion` / `inverted_axis_line`) feeds the triad and the sheet. The CPS copy is documented in the decision record. No unwrap/expect/panic in the new Rust code.
- Provenance lines are present. Files stay within the 400-line law (the CPS files are exempt). Display only, so no command is needed. No build.rs, .github or dependency changes.

## Local results (merged with current origin/main, clean auto-merge)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app setup_sheet / inverted_post / inverted_equivalence / axis_direction | 7 / 15 / 2 / 12 pass |
| app posting / golden_cl / conformance / inverted_axis_display | 17 / 23 / 6 / 5 pass |
| app machine / fanuc_post / post_not_judged | 32 / 8 / 4 pass |
| camcraft-post (all suites) | pass |
| camcraft-ui --lib (CWD crates/ui) | 307 pass, 2 ignored |
| clippy -D warnings, post + app + ui, --all-targets | clean |

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- The triad note offset is a fixed uv drop, so it is checked by position and not by eye (the PR says so).
- Draft PR: it is a `feat`, so it merges at the cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
